messages:
sam: quick heads-up — noticed a ~15% regression in end-to-end p99 for short prefix workloads after yesterday's cache change :thinking:

jess: ugh. which cache change? the move to segmented shards? :eyes:

sam: yeah, the prefix-cache sharding PR (shard count = 8) + new eviction heuristics. metric spike around 22:30 UTC.

linh: can you paste the query/profile that shows the p99? i want to see kv hit vs miss distribution.

sam: copied from dashboards:

```
metric: runtime.kv_prefix_cache.hit_rate
window: 1h
before: 0.86 -> after: 0.72

metric: runtime.request.p99_ms{workload:short_prefix}
before: 78ms -> after: 90ms
```

dave: fragmentation maybe? sharding increases per-shard fragmentation when eviction becomes unbalanced.

jess: good call. sam — can you run the per-shard hit-rate breakdown? `curl` to the /metrics-debug endpoint is easiest.

sam: running now, will paste output. potentionally noisy.

perf-bot: starting scrape of /metrics-debug?shard=all (invoked by sam)

sam: raw snippet:

```
shard_0: hit_rate=0.71, size=1.2G, evictions=432
shard_1: hit_rate=0.73, size=1.1G, evictions=12
shard_2: hit_rate=0.70, size=1.3G, evictions=489
shard_3: hit_rate=0.95, size=200M, evictions=0
shard_4: hit_rate=0.68, size=1.25G, evictions=511
shard_5: hit_rate=0.88, size=850M, evictions=34
shard_6: hit_rate=0.67, size=1.4G, evictions=600
shard_7: hit_rate=0.90, size=300M, evictions=2
```

linh: wow — very skewed. some shards nearly empty, others overloaded and heavily evicting. that explains fragmentation + increased misses.

jess: are keys evenly distributed? was the hash function changed in the PR?

sam: PR switched from FNV -> xxhash64 for perf, but partitioning logic stayed (key % shard_count). maybe distribution properties differ.

dave: non-uniformity could also be due to hot prefixes (many similar keys routed to same shard). we should correlate prefix namespace -> shard mapping.

sam: I ran a heatmap: top-100 prefixes -> shard mapping shows 63% of top prefixes land on shards 2,4,6.

jess: short-term mitigation: reduce shard_count to 4 or increase cache size per node to absorb evictions. long-term: consistent hashing to balance hot keys.

linh: agreed. can we try a canary: revert to FNV on one node and compare? or flip shard_count on a replica set?

sam: I can spin a canary tomorrow morning. timeline: 30m to deploy a single-node config tweak.

dave: also propose adding per-prefix quotas so one prefix can't trash a shard.

jess: file a small design doc for per-prefix caps (link please). for now, let's: 1) schedule canary revert to FNV, 2) run simulation with consistent hashing locally, 3) increase cache size by 15% as emergency buffer.

sam: will do 1 & 3 in the morning. i'll drop results here. thanks :white_check_mark:

perf-bot: created ticket #INF-872: "kv prefix cache shard imbalance investigation" assigned to sam, linch, dave.

linh: thanks — if anyone else wants to eyeball the heatmap i'll post link to grafana in thread.

jess: tagging @dave to help with the simulation harness.

dave: on it — will run a few synthetic workloads against the local sim and share latency histograms.

sam: sharing grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/kv-prefix-heatmap?orgId=1

jess: great. let's regroup after the canary results tomorrow. short checklist: canary revert, emergency cache bump, sim runs.

linh: ack. i'll draft the per-prefix cap doc and ping y'all.

sam: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick follow-up. keep updates concise here.
